name: Seated Leg Curl
summary: An isolation machine exercise that targets the hamstrings by flexing the knees from a seated position.

setup: Adjust the backrest so your knees align directly with the machine's pivot axis.
Position the lower leg pad just beneath your calves, above the Achilles tendons.
Lower and lock the thigh pad snugly against the top of your quadriceps to anchor your pelvis and thighs.
Grasp the handles firmly and sit tall with your lower back supported against the backrest.
steps: Flex your knees to curl the lever arm down and back as far as comfortable.
Pause briefly at peak contraction while squeezing your hamstrings.
Control the weight back up through a full range of extension without letting the weight stack slam.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you curl your legs downward; inhale as you return to the starting position.
cues: Pull your heels toward your glutes.
Keep your hips firmly seated in the chair.
Control the stretch on the way up.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the thighs or hips to rise off the seat during the curl.
common_faults.correction: Secure the lap pad firmly against your thighs and pull up on the handles to brace your body.

common_faults.fault: Knee axis misaligned with the machine pivot point.
common_faults.correction: Adjust the seat back until the lateral condyle of the knee is in line with the machine's axis of rotation.

common_faults.fault: Using momentum and cutting the eccentric phase short.
common_faults.correction: Control the return movement under tension until your knees are almost fully extended.

precautions: Ensure the thigh pad is securely locked before initiating the set to prevent pelvic lifting.
